key_insight: A self-supervised safety measure can learn collision risk directly from large-scale naturalistic driving data without crash labels, providing accurate real-time warnings that give vehicles extra time to react before crashes or near-crashes.
problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity and bias of labeled crash data and the lack of a generalized, scalable safety metric for proactive collision prediction in autonomous and assisted driving systems.
method: Train models on large-scale naturalistic driving sequences using label-free (self-/unsupervised) objectives to infer latent risk signals from everyday driving behavior.
Derive a continuous risk score that rises prior to crashes and near-crashes, enabling real-time alerts and evaluation against recorded incidents.
Validate at scale on naturalistic datasets to show earlier and more reliable warnings compared with conventional heuristics or limited supervised approaches.
impact: Enables scalable, data-driven safety assessment and real-time collision warnings for AD/ADAS without costly annotation, improving deployment safety, monitoring, and continuous improvement of driving systems.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram showing risk score rising ahead of a crash (time-to-warning) with annotated reaction window
Pipeline schematic: naturalistic driving data → self-supervised model → continuous risk score → real-time alert
Comparative chart (e.g., CDF or ROC) showing earlier detection/greater recall vs baseline heuristics
Map/heatmap of high-risk segments or clusters extracted from large-scale driving data
paper_title: Learning collision risk proactively from naturalistic driving data at scale
paper_authors: Yiru Jiao, Simeon C. Calvert, Sander van Cranenburgh, Hans van Lint
